summary: Hot Spring County, AR lookout known only from a Central US Lookouts page that names it; no build, design, staffing or present-state source found.

evidence.supports: lookout named Bismarck in Hot Spring County
Arkansas had 122 known fire towers at the height of operation
evidence.quote: At the height of their operation, Arkansas had 122 known fire towers.
In 1994, forty-eight still stood, but it is unknown if any were still in use.

evidence.supports: the named list of fourteen ends with Tall Peak, and Bismarck is not on it

evidence.supports: watchmen often lived in or near their towers and scanned for smoke
evidence.quote: Tower watchmen often lived alone in or near the tower and spent the daylight hours scanning the forests for signs of smoke.

notes_for_editor: The only source naming this lookout is the Central US Lookouts page, which gives the name and Hot Spring County and nothing else. Two web searches and a check of the cached NHLR and FFLOS pages found no other record. The record's coordinates (34.3525, -93.1572) come from that site's map widget and are unchecked against any other source, and the record's kind 'tower' is not stated on the page. The story is short because the evidence is; it has no build, design, staffing or fate. Worth checking Arkansas Forestry Commission or Hot Spring County historical records before any expansion. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story's 'Bismarck is not among them' rests on the Encyclopedia's named list of fourteen, now quoted at both ends.
